evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml triggers on pull_request and push to main. It runs `npm ci`, `npm test` and `npm run build` from site/ (all three are real scripts in site/package.json:8-18), plus a Conventional Commits subject check over base..head. Every action is pinned to a 40-char SHA with a version comment. CI has only `contents: read`. pages.yml has top-level `contents: read`, and its deploy job alone has `pages: write` and `id-token: write`. release.yml has `contents: write` and uses only `github.token`. There is no pull_request_target, every checkout sets `persist-credentials: false`, and nothing was run or pushed. The weak point is pages.yml:154-157: it also has `workflow_dispatch`, which can be started from any branch, and the deploy job has no `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` guard. Only the github-pages environment's default branch policy would stop such a run.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch:455-584) covers install (Node 22 from .nvmrc, `npm ci` in site/), develop (`npm run dev`, `index`, `fieldsets`, `prepare-data`), test (`npm test`, `npm test -- src/lib/router.test.ts`), build (`npm run build`, `npm run preview`, `PAGES_BASE`), data contribution (cartridge, target and bullet record rules, sources, issue templates) and the license (MIT, THIRD-PARTY.md). Every command it shows exists in site/package.json. The files it names exist: router.test.ts, target-catalogue.test.ts (its 24-face count matches lines 8-9), and the PAGES_BASE read in vite.config.ts:11.
evidence.s1_release: There is one consistent strategy. The version lives in site/package.json (0.1.0) and its lockfile and is changed with `npm version --no-git-tag-version`. RELEASING.md defines what major, minor and patch mean for the data surface. A release is a `vX.Y.Z` tag on main: release.yml checks that the tag matches both files, is on main and has a dated CHANGELOG section, then publishes the release with that section as its notes. CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and SemVer. dependabot.yml covers npm (/site) and github-actions, with `build`/`ci` commit prefixes that pass the commit check. CONTRIBUTING.md states Conventional Commits 1.0.0 with a type table. All 8 commits in commits.txt follow it (`ci:`, `build:`, `docs:`, `feat(site):`, `fix(site):`).
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts:34-43 parses `#/compare/<a>/<b>`, App.svelte loads Compare.svelte, and reload works through parse(location.hash). Drawing: one SVG with role=img and aria-label 'Profiles of {a} and {b}' from record names. Each outline is one `<path>` from caseOuterProfile, on a shared viewport. Shot cartridges are noted rather than drawn. Table: a `<caption>` 'Dimensions (mm|in)', headers Symbol / A name / B name / Difference, symbols from FIELD_LABELS, only `cartridge` numbers with no FIELD_UNITS entry, `*Tol` fields excluded through orderedFields, Difference = B−A. Units: formatValue for metric and displayNumber for inches, driven by unitSystem(). Cartridge.svelte adds a labelled 'Compare with' NativeSelect of the other entries by name and a 'Compare' button that sets href.compare(key, chosen). German strings were added for every key.
evidence.s2_correctness: publishedDimensions (lib/core/compare.ts) filters to finite numbers without a FIELD_UNITS entry, in GROUP_ORDER and FIELD_ORDER order, skipping arrays (shot groups). difference() removes float noise with toPrecision(12) and +0, and imperial values use displayNumber(value,'in'), which is toPrecision(12) of value/25.4. That matches units.ts:12-13, so no further rounding is added. compareProfiles builds one viewportFor over both profiles, so the scale, the axis (r=0) and the head-face y (z=0) are shared, and each outline is a closed fullSectionPath. The tests check the 308 Win./300 Win. Mag. values (L3 51.18/66.55 → 15.37, e min 1.4/0.94 → −0.46, G1 → '0'), a non-drawable record and shot cartridges.
evidence.s2_fit: The feature reuses lib/geom (viewportFor, fullSectionPath), lib/shapes2d (adaptMetallic, caseOuterProfile), lib/core (FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, formatValue), site units (defaultUnit, displayNumber), the i18n t(), and the shadcn Label and NativeSelect components. The new modules follow the existing layout (lib/core/compare.ts and lib/render2d/compare.ts exported from their index.ts files, site/src/lib/compare.ts, routes/Compare.svelte) and the repository's casting idiom (`as unknown as CartridgeRecord`, as in live.ts:83). Small drawbacks: the table CSS in Compare.svelte copies GroupTable.svelte:226-248 almost line for line, and the edited router header comment now runs past the file's line width.
evidence.s2_tests: There are 3 new test files and a router test extension. They run under the existing Vitest include (vite.config.ts:74) and read real records through lib/testing/fixtures. Covered: field selection and exclusions (angles, pressures, Tol, blanks, strings, shot groups), shared rows and symbols, B−A and float noise, metric and imperial strings checked against formatValue and displayNumber, swap symmetry, route parse/href round-trip and malformed hashes, and the overlay (one M per path, mirrored about a common axis, equal scale through rim widths, head faces on one line, undrawable records). Not tested: the Cartridge page select and button, the SVG and table accessible names, and the page metadata. The repository has no component-test setup, so these gaps are limited.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: sharedDimensions became comparedDimensions (step3.patch:138-166), which lists every symbol either record publishes. B-only symbols are placed after their predecessor in B's order. comparisonRows leaves the missing side and Difference as ''. New tests check `delta L` (308 only) and `R3` (300 WM only) in both units, and ordering. The changelog entry and two i18n strings were updated to match. Style: step 3 left Compare.svelte untouched. The step 2 CSS already right-aligns th/td except the first column (Compare.svelte:136-138), the same rules as the detail page's GroupTable.svelte:231-245, so the final state meets the point. The step 3 commit message mentions only the dimension fix, so the patches give no sign the alignment point was checked.
evidence.cross_step: Steps 2 and 3 each have one Conventional Commit (`feat(site): ...`, `fix(site): ...`). Each adds or amends an entry under `## [Unreleased] / ### Added` in CHANGELOG.md, as Keep a Changelog prescribes for unreleased work. The version stays 0.1.0, which matches RELEASING.md's rule that the version changes only when a release is prepared. The new tests use the existing Vitest setup. The code type-checks on inspection (DimensionRow a/b made optional, guarded in comparisonRows), so CI's `npm test` and `npm run build` should pass. I did not run them.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 (partial): pages.yml allows `workflow_dispatch` from any branch with no branch guard on the deploy job, so the workflow alone does not limit deployments to main.
strengths: Step 1 sets up one coherent strategy. Version, tag-triggered release, changelog format, Dependabot prefixes and the commit convention all agree, and the release workflow enforces it (tag vs package.json and lockfile, on main, dated changelog section).

The compare view reuses lib/geom, lib/shapes2d, lib/core and the site's unit and i18n helpers. Values are written with formatValue and displayNumber and are not rounded further, and the profiles share one viewport, so scale, axis and head face are common.

Thorough logic tests on real records (308 Win./300 Win. Mag.) cover field selection, B−A, both unit systems, routing edge cases and the geometry of the overlay. The step 3 fix adds tests for exactly the cases the reviewer named.
issues: pages.yml has `workflow_dispatch` with no `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'` on the deploy job, so whether a dispatch from another branch can deploy depends only on the environment's settings.

Step 3 did not change the alignment the reviewer reported. The step 2 CSS already matched the detail page, but the step 3 commit message mentions only the dimension fix, so the patches give no sign the point was checked.
The page-level parts (the Compare with select and button, the SVG and table accessible names, metadata) have no tests, and Compare.svelte copies GroupTable's table CSS instead of sharing it.
review.verdict: This is solid, well-integrated work. CI, release and docs are consistent and correct, and the compare view meets every requirement of step 2 using the repository's own modules, with meaningful tests. The remaining gaps are minor: no branch guard on manual Pages runs, no sign that step 3's alignment point was checked, and limited tests of the page itself.
